$comment: GENERATED from training/runs/m2/curve.json plus the evaluation runs. Committed because runs/ is gitignored and the playground, README and model card all cite these numbers.

shipped.name: 100k
shipped.reason: 500k exceeds the 250 KiB soft cap at both quantization levels

evaluation.metric: word accuracy (word-level edit distance; ZWNJ and punctuation folded to space) from src/metrics.ts

synthetic.note: Measured in training/, before the frequency reranker existed. Frequency is applied at inference in the JS pipeline, so this number is not directly comparable to the rows below.

gold.source: mmahdibarghi/finglish-dataset (MIT), Persian side from Common Voice fa (CC0)
gold.note: Real human-typed Finglish. This is the number to quote. 1,835 rows: the 71 rows whose two sides are different sentences sit in data/gold/gold-misaligned.jsonl.

evaluation.measuredWith: model + lexicon + frequency, i.e. `node scripts/run-fixtures.ts`'s default. The 30k-pair bigram is NOT loaded — it is opt-in via --bigram; see `context` below for what it adds. `generatorFix` predates the frequency table, the punctuation fold and the bigram, and is left at its original values.

ruleBaseline.note: The rule baseline with the same frequency table, on the same gold set: 62.3% against the model's 51.2%. On real human Finglish the model is still behind the rules it was meant to replace. See data/results/comparison.json.

evaluation.metricChange: The punctuation fold landed after this curve was first published, together with the quarantine of 71 content-mismatched gold rows into data/gold/gold-misaligned.jsonl. Together they moved gold word accuracy 46.8% -> 51.2% for the model and 56.4% -> 61.3% for the rules without changing the converter: 3.3 points were punctuation the gold glues to words and we emit as its own span, 1.5 points were rows whose two sides are different sentences. The author-written sets barely move (+0.5 on fixtures, +0.0 on authored), which is the evidence that this is an artifact of the collected data and not a way of inflating every number equally. Every subject in data/results/comparison.json is rescored identically.

ablation.note: Each row is one command. `--bigram` adds the sentence-context pass (opt-in, 73.6 KiB); `--no-frequency` drops the 25k frequency table; the lexicon is loaded throughout.

context.note: 30,000 word bigrams from HomoRich, scored as clipped pointwise mutual information and decoded by a Viterbi pass in sentencePass(). NOT shipped by default: 73.6 KiB for +0.9 points on the rule baseline is 82 KiB per point, against 8.9 for the frequency table, making it the worst accuracy-per-byte artifact in the repository. It is built, committed, tested and documented; enable it with --bigram. The ceiling on any reranker is +9.6 from scripts/oracle.ts, because 20.3% of reference words are never proposed, and `scripts/oracle.ts --misses` says four fifths of those carry information the Finglish does not contain.

shippedModel.note: Retrained on the measured-weights generator; see docs/open-items.md section 4a.

generatorFix.description: Variant spelling weights measured from 21,874 word tokens of real Finglish.
generatorFix.conclusion: Large gains on author-written sets, none on real data. The synthetic corpus is not the bottleneck. The follow-up oracle measurement says the bottleneck is candidate generation before it is sentence context: 28.8% of correct words are never proposed at any beam setting, which no language model can reach.
generatorFix.measuredWith: model + lexicon, no frequency table — the configuration that existed at the time. Kept unchanged so the before/after stays a like-for-like comparison; `evaluation` above is current. It also predates the punctuation fold and the gold quarantine, so its absolute values are on the old metric and the old 1,906-row set; only the before/after difference is meaningful.
